gap: No result ChatGPT got says that QNAP is the only one of the five NAS makers to put a number on its CGNAT relay speed: myQNAPcloud Link relay traffic is 'usually limited to 1-2 Mbps', so 1 GB of phone video takes about 67–133 minutes. Synology, Asustor, TerraMaster and UGREEN only say their relays are slower or bandwidth-limited, and give no figure.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat has no search results and no cited pages. Its answer is a table marking every brand 'Yes' for 'Works behind CGNAT?' with no throughput behind the yes. Our current page has the 1–2 Mbps figure, but it links it to QNAP's support FAQ. I opened that FAQ on 2026-11-17 and it gives no number, only 'we will monitor the bandwidth and enforce some limits if necessary'. The number is in QNAP's Qfile Pro reference article dated 2026-04-07. Nothing the shopper saw lines up the five relays in the same unit or notes that four makers publish no cap.
decides: This partly settles the pick. QNAP's built-in relay is out for phone photo and video backup behind CGNAT, because its own stated 1–2 Mbps (0.125–0.25 MB/s) works for browsing files but not for moving video. QNAP owners on CGNAT need Tailscale in Container Station or a direct route. The other four makers publish no relay cap, so they can't be ranked on speed. The real split is direct path versus relay. Synology tries a hole-punched direct path before falling back to its relay. UGREEN tries IPv6 P2P first, which matters on Starlink and 5G home internet where IPv6 is often present. For heavy phone backup, the safe recommendation on any brand is Tailscale, whichever maker it is. The page should stop presenting 'Works behind CGNAT: Yes' as if it meant the same thing for every brand.

findings.label: Relay throughput stated by maker
findings.source_title: Qfile Storage Speed Reality: Why is Direct Connection faster than Relay Server? (QNAP, 2026-04-07)
findings.note: QNAP's wording: 'bandwidth is usually limited to 1-2 Mbps' on the myQNAPcloud Link relay route, because global users share the relay. Qfile Pro labels this route 'myQNAPcloud Link (Relay Mode)' and labels DDNS/WAN IP 'Direct Connection Mode'. Arithmetic: 1 GB = 8,000 Mb; 8,000 ÷ 2 = 4,000 s ≈ 67 min; 8,000 ÷ 1 = 8,000 s ≈ 133 min.

findings.label: Relay limit in QNAP's support FAQ
findings.value: QNAP says it 'will monitor the bandwidth and enforce some limits if necessary'; DDNS (direct) has 'no bandwidth limit'
findings.source_title: myQNAPcloud Help FAQ: Are there bandwidth limits when using the myQNAPcloud remote access service?
findings.note: This FAQ has no Mbps figure. Our current page cites this URL for '1–2 Mbps', which is wrong. Move the citation to the Qfile reference article above. DDNS does not help on CGNAT because there is no inbound IPv4.

findings.label: Relay limits stated by maker
findings.value: Tries LAN IP / EZ-Router first, then the relay; on cloud.ezconnect.to 'ASUSTOR will limit bandwidth speed'; 'Some applications cannot be executed in this mode'
findings.note: The page gives no Mbps figure and does not say which apps fail on the relay. It recommends the ASUSTOR EZ Connect client for large transfers.

findings.label: Relay behaviour stated by maker
findings.value: Relayed connections 'may be slower than port-forwarded connections because of increased network latency'; relay 'may not work in some regions because of restrictions imposed by specific Internet service providers'
findings.source_title: Network and External Access | DSM 7.4 software specifications | Synology
findings.note: Synology blames latency, not a bandwidth cap, and states no Mbps figure. The spec page also says third-party apps and services that need direct IP/DDNS mapping are not supported over QuickConnect, and admins choose which apps are reachable.

findings.label: Remote access without a public IP (maker)
findings.value: UGREENlink 'can provide remote access without requiring you to obtain a public IP address'; works from the UGREEN NAS mobile app and desktop client using the UGREENlink ID
findings.source_title: How to Access Your UGREEN NAS Remotely: UGREENlink, DDNS, and Tailscale (UGREEN, 17/04/2026)
findings.note: This UGREEN page gives no relay speed or cap and does not describe P2P versus relay. The IPv6-P2P-then-relay order is in UGREEN support article 671, which I could not open (see unsourced).

findings.label: How TNAS.online works (maker doc)
findings.value: Remote access 'without the need for port forwarding' via browser (TNAS.online/<TNAS ID>), TNAS mobile (Android/iOS) and TNAS PC; needs a TerraMaster account; Security Isolation Mode must be off
findings.note: The TOS 7 doc does not say whether traffic is relayed or peer-to-peer and states no bandwidth figure.
